title: 2024 budget public consultation night
subtitle: Delegates spoke on cycling infrastructure, traffic calming and the future of the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony grant.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a special meeting to hear public input on the proposed 2024 budget. No motions were recorded other than adjournment, so the committee made no recommendations. Staff opened by noting that Final Budget Day is scheduled for December 14, 2023, and that an online survey on strategic priorities was open for one more day.

Four delegates were registered. Three spoke in person or online about cycling and active transportation, including a young resident, a local employer and a cycling advocacy group. They supported funding for completing the downtown cycling grid, better wayfinding and traffic calming. A fourth delegate, speaking for the arts community, asked the City to keep the annual Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony grant of $372,626 in the budget while the orchestra restructures.

The feedback becomes part of the public record ahead of the mayor's budget proposal and Council's final budget decisions. A further delegate who was unavailable on the night is expected to be heard at a later special council meeting.
debate: Cycling supporters argued that connected, separated bike lanes and trails make riding safer and more usable, and that gaps and road crossings keep people driving or taking limited transit.
One delegate said cycling spending is small next to annual road reconstruction costs and can reduce road wear and the need for future road expansion.

The cycling advocacy group urged keeping the funds and timelines for the downtown cycling grid, more paved trails and traffic-calmed crossings, and asked whether the large road reconstruction budget includes cycling and traffic calming.

The arts delegate asked the City to keep the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony grant, conditional on the orchestra restructuring and preparing for a next season, and described several separate organizations working on its revival.

In response, the mayor said the City continues to talk with the bankruptcy trustee and the symphony foundation, since the symphony's home is a City-owned venue, and with parties who share the delegate's aims.
